Rajen Babu.description: Rajen Babu is a kindly, elderly man living in Darjeeling, known for his amiable nature and interest in antiques; 'Babu' is a respectful suffix or title used for men in Bengal and is often attached to his name.

Tapesh Ranjan.description: The thirteen-year-old narrator and assistant to Feluda, also known by the nickname Topshe.

Feluda.description: A sharp and observant private detective and cousin to Topshe, whose full name is Prodosh C. Mitter.

Tinkori Babu.description: A mystery writer and tenant in Rajen Babu’s house, revealed to be Tinkori Mukhopadhyay, who possesses a penchant for deduction.

Dr Phoni Mitra.description: A local doctor in Darjeeling, sometimes consulted by Rajen Babu, and a follower of the same guru.

Abanimohan Ghoshal.description: A collector of antiques and curios, suspected of ulterior motives regarding Rajen Babu’s possessions.

Prabeer Majumdar.description: Rajen Babu’s estranged son, who left home years ago and has recently returned from abroad.

Gyanesh.description: A friend of Rajen Babu who recommended Tinkori Babu as a tenant.

Mr Gilmour.description: The manager of a tea estate and a regular customer at the curio shop.

Mr Naulakha.description: Another regular buyer at the curio shop, currently away in Sikkim.

Mall.description: The main promenade or public walkway in Darjeeling, a popular gathering spot.

Nepali.description: Refers to people from Nepal or of Nepali origin, many of whom live and work in Darjeeling.

Tibetan.description: Relating to Tibet or its culture; Tibetan antiques and art are common in Darjeeling.

Calcutta.description: A major city in eastern India, now known as Kolkata.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, India, famous for its tea and scenic views.

Radha restaurant.description: A local restaurant in Darjeeling, used as a landmark.

Ananda Bazar.description: A well-known Bengali newspaper, referenced for its distinctive typeface.

Bankura.description: A town in West Bengal, India, where Rajen Babu attended missionary school.

Rangeet valley.description: A valley near Darjeeling, named after the Rangeet River.

Kanchenjunga.description: The third highest mountain in the world, visible from Darjeeling.

Mount Everest Hotel.description: A hotel in Darjeeling where Prabeer Majumdar is staying.

Central Hotel.description: Another hotel in Darjeeling, mentioned as a possible place of stay.

Observatory Hill.description: A notable hill in Darjeeling, known for its scenic views.

Nepal Curio Shop.description: A shop in Darjeeling selling antiques and curios, frequented by several characters.

Sikkim.description: A neighboring Indian state to Darjeeling, mentioned as Mr Naulakha's current location.

Planters’ Club.description: A social club in Darjeeling, historically frequented by tea estate managers.

Cart Road.description: A road in Darjeeling, where a wealthy businessman lives.

THE EMP ERO R’S RI NG.description: The title of the next story or chapter, appearing at the end of the text.

tankha.description: A Tibetan religious painting on cloth, often depicting Buddhist deities or scenes.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'hello' or 'goodbye,' accompanied by folded hands.

cheroot.description: A type of cigar with both ends clipped during manufacture, popular in South Asia.

guru.description: A spiritual teacher or guide in Indian religions.

curio.description: A rare or unusual object, often collected for its artistic or historical value.

muffler.description: A scarf worn around the neck for warmth, commonly used in India.

lozenge.description: A small, flavored medicinal tablet, often for soothing the throat.

mask.description: A face covering, often decorative or ceremonial, used here as a collectible item from the region.
